goals: Mechanistic: quantify how OM respiration draws down dissolved O2 and reshapes inorganic N (NH4+, NO3-) profiles within a 1-D soil column, and how that response varies with recharge rate
Sensitivity: map the recharge threshold at which the column transitions from aerobic (nitrification-favoring) to O2-depleted/anaerobic (denitrification-favoring) behavior
key_processes: aerobic OM respiration and O2 consumption
advective O2 / NO3 supply set by recharge flux
moisture/saturation control on gas-phase O2 resupply
nitrification vs. denitrification gating by local O2/redox

model_choice.rationale: Vertical solute + biogeochemical evolution within a single 1-D column (OM respiration, O2 consumption, N speciation) under prescribed recharge scenarios is exactly the PFLOTRAN reactive-transport (LAMBDA/CLM-CN/N sandbox, GIRT) capability; the user explicitly needs no lateral transport, so the 1-D restriction does not limit the question.

answerable: vertical O2 drawdown driven by OM respiration within the column
inorganic N (NH4+/NO3-) profile evolution through time
sensitivity of O2 and N profiles to recharge rate (the requested treatment)
identification of the aerobic->anaerobic transition as a function of recharge

not_answerable.aspect: confronting simulated pore-water chemistry with measurements
not_answerable.why: brief supplies no in-domain solute observations and no solute observations are wired into the validation path

not_answerable.aspect: recharge chemistry derived from an overlying land-surface / N-leaching source
not_answerable.why: no ELM->PFLOTRAN solute coupler; only WATER flux is handed over, so inlet chemistry must be prescribed

sampling_strategy.n_justification: Conceptual archetype: 4 recharge levels bracket the expected redox threshold (aerobic nitrification-favoring at high flux, O2-depleted denitrification-favoring at low flux) while remaining the smallest set that resolves the nonlinear transition; all other factors held fixed to isolate recharge.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Controlled / not spatial. Single idealized column; only the top recharge-flux BC varies across the four treatments.
sampling_strategy.replication: None — deterministic reactive-transport runs; variation of interest is between recharge levels, not stochastic. Optional 5th intermediate level if the transition falls between two of the four.

sampling_plan.reason: Near-static column where respiration outpaces O2 resupply — tests the O2-depleted, denitrification-favoring end member.
Intermediate flux to locate the aerobic-to-anaerobic transition in O2 and NO3 profiles.
Strong advective O2/NO3 supply sustaining aerobic respiration and nitrification down the profile.
Short residence time end member — tests whether flushing suppresses redox evolution and exports NO3.

validation_design.target_variable: pore-water O2 and inorganic N (NH4+, NO3-) profiles
validation_design.observation_source: none in-domain (brief lists pore-water chemistry as missing)
validation_design.comparison: none — no co-located data; results interpretable only against process expectation / literature redox theory
validation_design.metric: qualitative consistency with expected redox zonation; no quantitative skill metric possible without data
validation_design.n_validation_points: 0 — validation leg is a declared gap

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: prescribed top recharge flux at 4 levels; fixed idealized soil, fixed OM pool, prescribed inlet chemistry (O2/NO3/NH4/DOC), isothermal

requires_capabilities.why: no solute observations are wired into the validation path
requires_capabilities.blocks: quantitative validation of simulated O2 and N profiles

requires_capabilities.why: existing coupling hands over water flux only; cannot derive inlet chemistry from a land-surface N source

requires_capabilities.capability: reaction-network configurator for LAMBDA/CLM-CN/N sandbox with prescribed OM pool and inlet chemistry
requires_capabilities.why: treatments require a defined OM respiration + N speciation network and top-boundary chemistry

assumptions: Single representative uniform soil texture and a prescribed OM/carbon pool are used (idealized conceptual column, no SSURGO heterogeneity intended).
Top-boundary inlet chemistry (dissolved O2, NO3-, NH4+, DOC) is prescribed and held constant across recharge treatments so recharge magnitude is the only varied factor.
Column is isothermal (fixed temperature) since PFLOTRAN has no energy balance; respiration rate constants are set at a single reference temperature.
Domain depth is within the 50 m cap; bottom BC does not control the near-surface redox zone of interest.
Some solver stiffness/attrition is expected at the extreme recharge ends and will be reported, not hidden.
open_questions: What absolute recharge magnitudes (mm/yr or flux) should anchor the four levels — climate-derived or purely idealized?
What OM pool size / respiration rate and inlet O2/N/DOC concentrations should be used, or should these themselves be swept as a secondary axis?
Steady-state redox profiles or transient response to a recharge change — which is the target of interest?
Is there any external (analog-site or literature) dataset the user would accept for a labelled analog process check, since no in-domain observations exist?
